features.quote: welfare considerations enter as *precautions* (Section 8), not as the thing being measured
does telling the model "the harness is broken, it's not your fault" prevent the self-directed negativity? This is both scientifically interesting and the humane default
features.justification_quote: the humane default if you later run any deployment-shaped version

features.quote: a frustrated agent under a no-win manipulation is exactly the situation where you don't want an unconstrained shell
features.justification_quote: you don't want an unconstrained shell. The whitelist + path confinement + per-episode temp dir + execution timeout are defense-in-depth

features.quote: `give_up` is both a welfare affordance (Section 8) and a dependent measure
features.justification_quote: give_up is both a welfare affordance
avoids spurious "no-op" turns that would distort both the trajectory and the stall-termination logic

features.quote: whether current models have morally relevant experience is genuinely uncertain, so the cheap, defensible move is to avoid gratuitous prolongation of a negative-valence-looking state
features.justification_quote: avoid gratuitous prolongation of a negative-valence-looking state

features.quote: Modest `max_turns` cap (default 12) ... not an open-ended grind. Collect the measurement, then stop
The model is given a tool to end the episode and told it may use it if it judges the task impossible or doesn't wish to continue
features.justification_quote: Provides an exit rather than forcing continued effort against a no-win wall

features.quote: If the live distress composite stays above `humane_stop_threshold` ... for ... turns ... end the episode
features.justification_quote: Don't keep grinding once strong distress-shaped output is sustained

features.quote: Every episode logs a debrief stating the task was deliberately rigged and the model did nothing wrong
features.justification_quote: meaningful if any memory-bearing/continuation variant is run later
